Authors: Havlíček, V., Córcoles, A. D., Temme, K., Harrow, A. W., Kandala, A., Chow, J. M., & Gambetta, J. M.
Title: Supervised learning with quantum-enhanced feature spaces
Quantum_Method: Quantum Support Vector Classifier (QSVC) & Quantum Variational Classifier
Statistical_Evaluation: Error bars from quantum shot sampling
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that quantum fidelity kernels can classify engineered data designed to be hard for classical simulation with near-100% accuracy on hardware.
Identified_Gap: Evaluated only on 2D synthetic dataset engineered to match the quantum feature map; no real-world data or natural language text.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work evaluates real-world unstructured text across 3 datasets, multi-layer language embeddings (TF-IDF, RoBERTa, MiniLM, MPNet), dimensionality scaling (2D-16D), cross-source domain shift, and 10-seed paired equivalence testing.

Authors: Schuld, M., & Killoran, N.
Title: Quantum Machine Learning in Feature Hilbert Spaces
Main_Contribution: Formulated quantum machine learning with parameterized quantum states as a kernel method operating implicitly in exponential-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
Identified_Gap: Small toy datasets; focused on theoretical formalism rather than empirical NLP or robustness under domain shift.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We conduct an extensive empirical multi-dataset evaluation on security text with matched RBF controls, geometry diagnostics, and computational scaling.

Authors: Huang, H.-Y., Broughton, M., Mohseni, M., Babbush, R., Boixo, S., Neven, H., & McClean, J. R.
Title: Power of data in quantum machine learning
Dataset: Quantum Many-Body Physics, Engineered Discrete Log, Fashion-MNIST
Quantum_Method: Projected Quantum Kernel SVM vs Standard Fidelity Kernel
Classical_Baseline: RBF SVM, Classical Neural Networks (MLP), Random Forest
Representation: Physical spin states, tabular continuous, projected quantum states
Main_Contribution: Proved that when classical data is abundant, classical ML matches quantum kernels; quantum advantage requires geometric disparity (s_K << s_C) on hard quantum data.
Identified_Gap: Focused primarily on synthetic/engineered quantum physics problems; did not evaluate natural language processing or text security.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work tests text security datasets (SMS, CEAS, MeAJOR), testing whether representation engineering or domain shifts create quantum geometric advantage on real NLP data.

Authors: Thanasilp, S., Wang, S., Cerezo, M., & Holmes, Z.
Title: Exponential concentration in quantum kernel methods
Main_Contribution: Proved that unconstrained global fidelity quantum kernels exponentially concentrate to uniform constants as qubit count or circuit depth increases, causing exponential sample complexity.
Identified_Gap: Pure theory and synthetic numerical simulations; does not evaluate practical NLP or cybersecurity pipelines.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We empirically validate kernel concentration mechanisms on real NLP text security datasets across 10 random seeds and 4 embedding models.

Authors: Bowles, J., Ahmed, S., & Biamonte, J.
Title: Contextuality and the Geometry of Quantum Machine Learning
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that the inductive bias of quantum classifiers is governed by state-space geometry, entropy, and participation ratios in the embedding manifold.
Identified_Gap: Abstract quantum information theory; no application to natural language or security threat classification.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work applies geometric and spectral diagnostics directly to empirical text classification Gram matrices across real security datasets.

Authors: Kübler, J. M., Muandet, K., & Bousquet, O.
Title: The Inductive Bias of Quantum Kernels
Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 34:12661-12673)
Dataset: Synthetic Symmetries, Fashion-MNIST, UCI Benchmark Suite
Classical_Baseline: Matched RBF SVM, Polynomial SVM, Linear SVM
Main_Contribution: Proved that quantum kernels offer inductive bias advantages only when data geometry matches the symmetry groups generated by the quantum circuit generators.
Identified_Gap: Did not investigate complex text representation spaces (transformers) or cross-source domain shift.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate the representation-to-encoding interaction across multiple text embeddings and domain shifts with full computational cost profiling.

Authors: Glick, J. R., Gujarati, T. P., Corcoles, A. D., Kim, Y., Kandala, A., Gambetta, J. M., & Temme, K.
Title: Covariant quantum kernels for data with group symmetries
Representation: Discrete group representations / continuous vector orbits
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated provable quantum advantage in sample complexity when quantum kernels are explicitly constructed to respect the underlying group symmetry of the data.
Identified_Gap: Requires strict mathematical group structure; inapplicable to unstructured natural language text without known group symmetries.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work systematically investigates unstructured text representations where explicit algebraic symmetries do not exist.

Authors: Rahevar, K., Patel, S., & Shah, M.
Title: Quantum Kernels for Text Classification: A Statistical and Diagnostic Framework Revealing the Low-Data Regime
Dataset: SMS Spam, BBC News, IMDB Subsets
Classical_Baseline: Linear SVM, RBF SVM, Logistic Regression
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that quantum kernels can match or marginally exceed classical kernels specifically in extreme low-data regimes (N < 200), with advantage vanishing as training size increases.
Identified_Gap: Evaluated only static embeddings (GloVe/Word2Vec) and TF-IDF; did not evaluate transformer representations (RoBERTa/MiniLM/MPNet), cross-source domain shift, or FDR corrections.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our study addresses multi-dataset cybersecurity (SMS, CEAS email, MeAJOR email), transformer representations (RoBERTa, MiniLM, MPNet), cross-source domain transfer (Direction A/B), statevector entropy/rank diagnostics, 10-seed preregistered equivalence testing (ε=±0.01), and memory/runtime scaling profiling.

Authors: Garg, S., Ramakrishnan, S., & Biamonte, J.
Title: Quantum text classification with transformer embeddings
Main_Contribution: Showed that transformer embeddings compressed via PCA can be classified by quantum kernels with accuracy comparable to linear classical baselines on small benchmark sets.
Identified_Gap: Small sample sizes; only 3 seeds; lacked matched RBF SVM baselines at identical dimensions; omitted kernel geometry analysis.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We compare 4 distinct representations (TF-IDF, RoBERTa, MiniLM, MPNet), diagnose geometric failure mechanisms, and perform 10-seed matched RBF evaluations under domain shift.

Authors: Shukla, A., Raghuwanshi, M. M., & Joshi, P.
Title: Quantum NLP for Document Classification: A Comparative Study
Main_Contribution: Reported that QNLP syntactic models achieve competitive classification accuracy on small news categorization benchmarks.
Identified_Gap: Single random seed; no matched nonlinear classical baselines (RBF SVM omitted); no out-of-distribution evaluation.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We provide a 10-seed matched baseline audit, rigorous statistical significance tests, and out-of-distribution domain shift validation.

Authors: Di Sipio, R., Huang, M., Chen, S. Y.-C., Mangini, S., & Worring, M.
Title: Dawn of Quantum Natural Language Processing
Main_Contribution: Synthesized foundational QNLP paradigms, demonstrating grammar-aware sentence embeddings directly mapped to quantum tensor networks on NISQ devices.
Identified_Gap: Restricted to short synthetic sentences; lacks scalability to real-world email/document text.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work addresses full-scale real-world security corpora (emails, SMS) via dense and sparse embeddings rather than toy syntactic sentences.

Authors: Coecke, B., de Felice, G., Meichanetzidis, K., & Toumi, A.
Title: Foundations for Quantum Natural Language Processing
Main_Contribution: Formulated the mathematical equivalence between pregroup grammar string diagrams and quantum circuits for composition-based NLP.
Identified_Gap: Purely foundational; does not provide empirical benchmarking against competitive classical NLP systems.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We benchmark statistical and deep representation embeddings on large-scale real-world text classification.

Authors: Lorenzo, R., Coecke, B., & Felice, G.
Title: Syntax-aware Quantum Natural Language Processing
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that syntax-aware quantum circuits can classify sentence meaning with fewer parameters than bag-of-words classical models on small synthetic corpora.
Identified_Gap: Small synthetic data; does not scale to practical multi-thousand sample text security corpora.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our study addresses the statistical/embedding branch of QNLP on large-scale security datasets with frozen splits and rigorous baselines.

Authors: Cybersecurity & QML Research Consortium (Systematic Review)
Title: Quantum Machine Learning for Phishing Detection: A Systematic Review of Current Techniques, Challenges, and Future Directions
Dataset: Analyzed 38 primary studies across UCI Phishing, Enron, SMS Spam, PhiUSIIL
Quantum_Method: QSVM / QSVC (45%), VQC / QNN (40%), Hybrid / Ensembles (15%)
Classical_Baseline: SVM, Random Forest, Logistic Regression (Frequently untuned)
Representation: Tabular URL features (55%), BoW/TF-IDF (35%), Word Embeddings (10%)
Statistical_Evaluation: Formal statistical hypothesis testing reported in only 8% of studies
Domain_Shift: 0% of reviewed papers evaluated out-of-distribution or cross-source transfer
Main_Contribution: Systematic review established that existing QML phishing literature suffers from severe benchmarking deficits: small subsampled datasets, lack of matched classical controls, zero external validation, and missing statistical tests.
Identified_Gap: Literature review synthesis; did not execute fresh empirical benchmarking.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work directly executes the rigorous benchmarking recommendations identified in this review: matched RBF controls, cross-source domain shift, frozen leakage-safe splits, 10-seed paired tests, and full runtime/memory profiling.

Authors: Guddanti, P., Al-Khafaji, A., & Sanyal, A.
Title: Detecting Phishing in Ethereum Networks using Quantum Machine Learning
Classical_Baseline: Random Forest, GBDT (XGBoost), Classical Linear/RBF SVM
Representation: Graph node structural & transaction tabular features
Main_Contribution: Showed that QRAC encoding improves false negative rates over ZZFeatureMap on IBM Heron hardware, though classical GBDT achieved superior overall F1.
Identified_Gap: Evaluated tabular graph transaction features; not natural language text; no domain-shift evaluation.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate natural language text security (emails, SMS) with language models, geometric diagnostics, and cross-source transfer.

Authors: Hridi, S. T., Islam, M. R., & Rahman, M. M.
Title: Batch-Wise Ensemble Evaluation of Classical SVM and Quantum SVM for Email Phishing Detection
Venue: IEEE Conference on Quantum Photonics & AI Networking (IEEE QPAIN 2026)
Main_Contribution: Claimed that an ensemble combining batch-wise QSVM and classical SVM improves email phishing detection over single models.
Identified_Gap: Single random seed; unmatched classical controls; no leakage audit; no domain shift.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work uses leakage-safe frozen splits, 10 random seeds, matched RBF controls, and out-of-distribution evaluation.

Authors: Shahriyar, S., Kabir, M. A., & Al-Mamun, A.
Title: PhishVQC: Optimizing Phishing URL Detection with Correlation Based Feature Selection and Variational Quantum Classifier
Venue: IEEE International Conference on Smart Applications, Communications and Computing (IEEE ISACC 2025)
Classical_Baseline: Linear SVM, Random Forest, Decision Tree
Representation: Handcrafted lexical and structural URL features (length, dots, symbols)
Main_Contribution: Claimed 96.5% accuracy using a 5-qubit VQC on heavily subsampled URL features.
Identified_Gap: Aggressive subsampling (800 of 235k samples); not text NLP; no matched full-scale comparison.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate full-scale NLP email/SMS corpora with matched dimensional controls and systematic multi-seed testing.

Authors: Al-Sarem, M., Al-Asali, M., Saeed, F., & Boulila, W.
Title: Quantum Support Vector Machine for Cybersecurity Threat Detection
Classical_Baseline: Linear SVM, Classical RBF SVM, Naive Bayes
Main_Contribution: Showed QSVM achieved comparable detection rates to classical RBF SVM on low-dimensional network traffic subsets.
Identified_Gap: Tabular intrusion data; small subsamples; did not evaluate language models or cross-network transfer.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our study addresses text security (phishing/spam) with high-dimensional language representations and domain transfer.

Authors: Lu, S., Lu, L. M., & Deng, D.-L.
Title: Quantum adversarial machine learning
Main_Contribution: Proved that quantum classifiers are inherently vulnerable to engineered adversarial perturbations in Hilbert space.
Identified_Gap: Continuous gradient-based perturbations; does not address discrete text perturbations (typos/synonyms).
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate natural distribution shifts across real phishing corpora rather than synthetic pixel attacks.

Authors: Li, X., Zhang, Y., & Wang, K.
Title: Large-scale empirical evaluation of quantum kernel methods across diverse tabular datasets
Classical_Baseline: Tuned RBF SVM, Random Forest, GBDT (XGBoost), MLP
Statistical_Evaluation: Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test & Paired Bootstrap CIs
Main_Contribution: Large-scale benchmark across 9 tabular datasets found no statistically significant advantage for quantum kernels over tuned RBF SVM (dataset explained 73% of variance).
Identified_Gap: Restricted strictly to tabular numerical datasets; no NLP, language representations, or domain-shift transfer.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our study addresses natural language text security, evaluating upstream transformer architectures, geometric failure modes, and out-of-distribution domain transfer.

Authors: Meyer, N., Scherer, P., & Plinge, A.
Title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning: Opportunities and Pitfalls
Main_Contribution: Formulated guidelines for rigorous QML benchmarking: identical data preprocessing, strictly matched dimensionality, multi-seed statistical testing, and reproducible splits.
Identified_Gap: Methodological guide; does not provide a specialized text security benchmark.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We implement and execute these benchmarking standards on full-scale text security applications.

Authors: Shaydulin, R., & Wild, S. M.
Title: Importance of Kernel Bandwidth in Quantum Machine Learning
Dataset: UCI Benchmark Suite (Sonar, Ionosphere, Breast Cancer)
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that feature scaling and angular bandwidth c drastically alter quantum kernel performance, often turning apparent quantum advantage into classical parity when RBF is properly tuned.
Identified_Gap: Evaluated only tabular UCI benchmarks; omitted natural language and transformer embeddings.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate angular mapping interactions specifically across dense transformer representations and sparse lexical features.

Authors: Abbas, A., Sutter, D., Zoufal, C., Lucchi, A., Figalli, A., & Woerner, S.
Title: The power of quantum neural networks
Main_Contribution: Introduced effective dimension as an information-theoretic capacity measure, proving quantum neural models can achieve higher capacity than comparable classical networks.
Identified_Gap: High capacity does not guarantee generalization on unstructured classical data without aligned inductive bias.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work measures effective rank and alignment on real text security Gram matrices, showing high capacity can coincide with noise in the absence of metric alignment.

Authors: Devlin, J., Chang, M.-W., Lee, K., & Toutanova, K.
Title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
Main_Contribution: Pre-trained bidirectional transformer encoders fundamentally transformed NLP by generating rich contextual token and sequence representations.
Identified_Gap: Classical foundation; high dimensional (768D) representations require compression for NISQ quantum feature maps.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate how compressing these contextual representations into low-dimensional subspaces interacts with quantum Hilbert space encodings.

Authors: Reimers, N., & Gurevych, I.
Title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
Classical_Baseline: InferSent, Universal Sentence Encoder, RoBERTa CLS
Representation: Siamese / Triplet pooled dense sentence vectors
Main_Contribution: Siamese fine-tuning maps sentences into semantically meaningful Euclidean vector spaces where cosine distances reflect semantic similarity.
Identified_Gap: Classical embedding architecture; does not consider quantum phase wrapping.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: Our work investigates the interaction between Sentence-BERT Euclidean manifolds and quantum fidelity kernels.

Authors: Song, K., Tan, X., Qin, T., Lu, J., & Liu, T.-Y.
Title: MPNet: Masked and Permuted Pre-training for Language Understanding
Venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 33:16843-16854)
Representation: Masked and permuted unified token embeddings (768D)
Main_Contribution: MPNet achieves superior classical representation quality by combining masked language modeling with permuted language modeling.
Identified_Gap: Does not evaluate quantum kernel transformations.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We uncover the critical scientific finding that MPNet's tight contrastive clustering causes destructive phase wrapping when mapped to cyclic quantum fidelity kernels.

Authors: Al-Sallami, M., Al-Ghamdi, A., & Farooq, M.
Title: Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning for SMS Phishing Detection Under Distribution Shift
Venue: ACM Transactions on Privacy and Security (ACM TOPS 26(4):1-28)
Dataset: SMS Spam, British Phishing Feed, Singapore Smishing Corpus
Classical_Baseline: LightGBM, Linear SVM, RoBERTa Classifier, Naive Bayes
Main_Contribution: Demonstrated that classical ML and transformer models suffer severe performance degradation (15% to 35% drop in F1) under cross-source distribution shifts in phishing security.
Identified_Gap: Purely classical cybersecurity study; did not evaluate quantum algorithms.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We evaluate whether quantum fidelity kernels offer any inherent inductive robustness advantage under identical text security domain shifts (finding: they do not, suffering greater relative degradation than classical RBF).

Authors: Cortes, C., Mohri, M., & Rostamizadeh, A.
Title: Algorithms for Learning Kernels Based on Centered Alignment
Classical_Baseline: Standard SVM with Unaligned RBF / Polynomial Kernels
Statistical_Evaluation: Concentration of measure bounds for kernel alignment
Main_Contribution: Proved that centered kernel-target alignment tightly bounds the generalization performance of kernel classifiers, providing theoretical guarantees for alignment-based kernel selection.
Identified_Gap: Classical kernel theory; does not treat quantum Hilbert spaces.
How_Our_Study_Addresses_The_Gap: We utilize centered alignment to diagnose why quantum kernels fail on contrastive sentence representations.
